sections.content:
Clicking the dot didn't do anything. Let me think about the merge rule more carefully.
Level 1: dots at (18,17), (18,23), (18,35), (24,41), (36,41) — all on the same board. Merges:
- t4: click (19,30): (17,23)→(29). The clicked cell (19,30) is the cell at col 29 (rows 18-21? no, the cell is 4x4: rows 18-21? hmm, level 1's cells: dot at (18,17) means the top-left of the 4x4 is (18,17). Cell size is 6 (17→23→29→35→41). So the cell at col 29 = rows 18-21, cols 29-32. Click (19,30) is inside it. The pair (17,23) merged into 29 (the empty cell to the right of the pair).
- t10: click (19,42): cell at col 41. Pair (29,35) → 41.
- t12: click (31,42): cell at row 30, col 41. Dots in col 41: (18,41), (24,41), (36,41). (18,41)+(24,41) are adjacent → merged into (30,41) = the cell below (24,41). Click (31,42) is inside cell (30,41). ✓
- t13: click (31,42) again: dots (30,41), (36,41) are adjacent → merged → level cleared.
So the rule: click the empty cell adjacent to two adjacent dots, and they merge into that cell. Level 1 cleared with 1 dot remaining.
Level 2: top board 3x7, dots at row 1: c1, c2, c4, c6. Bottom board 2x2, dot at (1,0).
Merging the top: (c1,c2)→c3; then (c3,c4)→c5; then (c5,c6)→c7?? But c7 doesn't exist (only 7 cols: c0..c6). Hmm! (c5,c6) are adjacent; the empty cell to the right of c6 doesn't exist. The empty cell to the left of c5 = c4 (now empty after merge). So (c5,c6) can merge into c4 (the cell to the left of the pair). The merge cell can be on either side.
So the top can be merged to 1 dot: c1c2→c3, c3c4→c5, c5c6→c4. Result: 1 dot at c4 (or somewhere).
That's exactly what I did at t22 → gray + key. So merging the top to 1 dot → both dots turn gray.
Why does the bottom dot also turn gray? Maybe because the level's goal state was reached, and gray = "complete," and the key = "collect/submit." But clicking the key reset it...
Wait a moment. Maybe I misidentified: clicking the key didn't reset — maybe it's a "next level" button, and the "reset" I saw was actually... no, the level is still 2, and the dots are back to the initial state. It was a reset.
Or: the key only works when the lock is at a specific position. When I clicked the key, the lock was at (51,13) = the bottom end of the track. What if the lock needed to be at the top end? Or in the middle?
Or: the key needs to be clicked when the merged top dot is at a specific cell (e.g., the gap cell c6)?
At t22, the merged top dot was at (15,31) = c4. The bottom dot was at (51,43) = (1,0).
Let me think about the lock's purpose. The lock moves along the track: positions (33,31)→(33,37)→(33,43)→(33,49)→(33,55)→(27,55)→(21,55)→(15,55) [top end] and (33,31)→(33,25)→(33,19)→(33,13)→(33,7)→(39,7)→(45,7)→(51,7)→(51,13) [bottom end].
The lock is like a "key" that unlocks gates. When the lock is at the top end (15,55), the top gate (gap) is unlocked. When it's at the bottom end (51,13), the bottom gate is unlocked.
The gaps align with the dot rows: top gap at row 1 (dot row), bottom gap at row 1 (dot row).
So: when the lock is at the top end, the dot at (1,6) can exit the top board through the gap onto the track. Then the dot moves along the track (the dot can be pushed along the track by arrow keys? or automatically?). Then it enters the bottom board through the bottom gap (when the lock is at the bottom end?).
But the dot is 4x4 and the track is 2px wide. The dot can't visually fit on the track... unless the dot teleports: click the dot at the gap while the lock is at the top end → the dot disappears from the top and appears at the bottom gap cell (1,1) of the bottom board.
When the lock was at the top end, I clicked the dot at (15,43) — nothing happened. Hmm.
Maybe the dot needs to be adjacent to the gap: the dot at c6 is adjacent to the gap (the gap is at cols 49-50, the dot's cell is cols 43-46; the border is cols 47-48). The dot is right next to the gap. Clicking the dot did nothing.
Maybe I need to click the gap while the dot is selected? Or click the dot and then click the gap?
Or maybe arrow keys move the dot when the dot is selected? In level 1, arrow keys moved the lock. But maybe arrow keys move the selected dot?
Let me test: click the dot at (15,43) to select it, then press RIGHT and see if the dot moves toward the gap.

<function=python>
<parameter=code>
def dots(f):
    out=[]
    for n in f.segmentation['nodes']:
        if n['color'] in ('N','g') and n['pixels']<20:
            b=n['boundary']; out.append((n['color'],min(p[0] for p in b), min(p[1] for p in b)))
    return sorted(out)
def lockpos(f):
    for n in f.segmentation['nodes']:
        if n['color']=='O':
            b=n['boundary']; return (min(p[0] for p in b), min(p[1] for p in b))

print('sel', lockpos(current_frame), dots(current_frame))
action(['RIGHT'])
print('R', lockpos(current_frame), dots(current_frame))
